title: Talking About Products
subtitle: Simple nouns and adjectives sales people use to describe what they sell
description: Learn the simple nouns and adjectives sales professionals use to describe products — like feature, quality, design, cheap, new, popular, and useful — when talking with customers.
dialogueSubtitle: Riley walks Dana through what makes Brightline's product stand out

vocabulary.definition: A part of a product that makes it useful or special.
vocabulary.example: One of our best features is the calendar that syncs with your team automatically.

vocabulary.definition: How good or bad something is.
vocabulary.example: Customers often mention the quality of our support team.

vocabulary.definition: The way something looks and works.
vocabulary.example: We updated the design last year to make it easier to use.

vocabulary.definition: The name and image of a company's products.
vocabulary.example: Brightline is a well-known brand in project management software.
Our starter plan is cheap enough for small teams just getting started.
We just launched a new tool for tracking deadlines.

vocabulary.definition: Liked or used by a lot of people.
vocabulary.example: The mobile app has become really popular with our customers.
The reminder tool is useful for teams that juggle a lot of projects.

phrasalVerbs.phrase: ONE OF THE BEST FEATURES IS
phrasalVerbs.definition: Point out a part of a product that you think customers will like most.
phrasalVerbs.example: One of the best features is the calendar that syncs automatically.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Tell someone what's included with a product.
phrasalVerbs.example: It comes with a free trial and full customer support.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Explain what sets a product apart from others.
phrasalVerbs.example: What makes it different is how easy it is for non-technical teams to use.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Share what people enjoy most about a product.
phrasalVerbs.example: Customers really like how quickly our support team responds.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Use this when explaining how a product is better or different from alternatives.
phrasalVerbs.example: Compared to other options, our pricing is hard to beat.

phrasalVerbs.definition: Suggest something to someone based on what they need.
phrasalVerbs.example: For a team your size, I'd recommend starting with the basic plan.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: So, Dana — since you're exploring Brightline for your team, let me walk you through a few [[features:a part of a product that makes it useful or special]] I think you'll like.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Perfect, I'd love that. What would you say is the best one?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Honestly, the [[design:the way something looks and works]] is what most people notice first — it's clean and easy to learn.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: That matters a lot for my team — half of them aren't very technical.

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: That's exactly why it's become so [[popular:liked or used by a lot of people]] with small agencies like yours.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: And how's the [[quality:how good or bad something is]] of the support, if something ever goes wrong?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Really strong — most questions get answered within the hour. We just released a [[new:made or introduced recently]] live-chat option too.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: That's reassuring. Is it [[cheap:costing little money]] enough for a team our size?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Our starter plan is actually one of the most affordable from any [[brand:the name and image of a company's products]] in this space.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Good to know. And would the reminder tool be [[useful:helpful; does a good job]] for a small team like mine?

dialogue.speaker: Riley
dialogue.text: Definitely — it's one of the things customers mention most when they tell us why they stay.

dialogue.speaker: Dana
dialogue.text: Sounds like exactly what we need. Let's set up a trial.

chooseResponse.instructions: Work in groups. Read the customer's line, then discuss which response (A, B, or C) is best. Choose your answer together, then click to see if you were right — and why.

options: They're all popular — it really depends on what you need.
Our Growth Plan is the most popular with small agencies — it has all the features most teams use every day.
I'd have to check our latest sales figures to be sure.
items.explanation: B is correct. It answers confidently and gives a specific reason why that option is popular. A avoids the question. C sounds unsure, which will make the customer less confident in you and your product.

items.customerLine: How is your brand different from the competition?
options: We're basically the same as the others, but cheaper.
I'm not really sure how we compare to other brands.
We're a well-known brand, but what makes us different is the design — it's the easiest tool in its category to learn.
items.explanation: C is correct. It leads with brand strength and follows with a concrete, specific differentiator. A undersells the product and sounds unprofessional. B shows a lack of product knowledge that will lose the customer's confidence.

items.customerLine: Is this a new product or has it been around a while?
options: We've been on the market for five years and just launched a new feature last month — so it's proven but always improving.
It's quite new, so there might be a few small issues still.
I think it's been around for a while — I'd have to check.
items.explanation: A is correct. It combines reliability (five years on the market) with freshness (new feature just launched). B creates unnecessary doubt. C sounds unprepared.

items.customerLine: Why should I pay more when cheaper options exist?
options: Honestly, the cheaper options are not very good.
The quality of our support and the design are what make the difference — customers really like how much time it saves them.
We can probably match the price if you need us to.
items.explanation: B is correct. It justifies the price with specific, customer-focused benefits. A criticises competitors, which looks unprofessional. C jumps straight to a discount before explaining any value, which weakens your position.

profileMatch.instructions: Read the three customer profiles. As a group, match each customer to the plan that best fits their needs. Be ready to explain your choices using words from this lesson — like 'feature', 'quality', and 'fit'. Click 'Reveal Matches' to check.

profiles.name: Leo
profiles.description: Leo runs a 4-person photography studio. He is on a tight budget and just needs a simple, useful tool to organise jobs and track payments. He does not need advanced features.

profiles.name: Nina
profiles.description: Nina manages a team of 18 at a digital marketing agency. She wants a tool with strong reporting features and good quality customer support. Her team needs to track client work and deals.

profiles.name: Marcus
profiles.description: Marcus is the COO of a 400-person logistics company. He needs a solution with a custom design, advanced integrations, and a dedicated account manager. Budget is not the main concern.

options.label: Starter Plan — $49/month
options.description: Basic project tracking and invoicing. Up to 5 users. Best for small teams or freelancers who need a simple, low-cost tool.

options.label: Growth Plan — $149/month
options.description: Deal tracking, customer management, and reporting. Up to 25 users. Best for growing teams that need to manage relationships and track results.

options.label: Enterprise Plan — Custom pricing
options.description: Unlimited users, custom integrations, dedicated account manager. Best for large companies that need a fully tailored solution.

finishTheLine.instructions: The salesperson's line has been cut off. As a group, discuss how you would finish it. Try to use vocabulary from this lesson. There is no single correct answer — compare your ideas, then click to see one possible answer.

items.customerLine: We've been using the same tool for years — I want something more modern.
items.salespersonStart: That's a great time to upgrade. One of our most popular new features is
items.suggestedCompletion: a real-time dashboard that shows exactly what your team is working on. The design is completely updated — most customers say it feels much faster to use.

items.customerLine: Is the quality really as good as you say?
items.salespersonStart: That's a fair question. Customers really like
items.suggestedCompletion: the quality of our support team — most questions are answered within the hour. We also have a 30-day trial, so you can see for yourself before you commit.

items.customerLine: I'm worried it might be too complicated for my team.
items.salespersonStart: I understand — the design is actually what most people mention first. It's
items.suggestedCompletion: built to be clean and easy to learn. Most teams are up and running within a day, even the ones who are not very technical.

items.customerLine: What makes your brand stand out from the others?
items.salespersonStart: What makes us different is that we focus on
items.suggestedCompletion: combining useful features with a design that is genuinely easy to learn. A lot of tools make you choose between powerful and simple — we think you should have both.
